uneven economic growth across regions. The world GDP grew at

sharper scrutiny, with decisions tied to clear business outcomes,
productivity gains, and cost optimisation.

as a significant source of uncertainty for the global economy,

trade flows. The conflict has led to volatility in oil and gas prices
due to supply risks and logistical constraints in critical transit
routes, which has translated into higher input costs across
industries and contributed to renewed inflationary pressures
in several economies. Elevated energy prices have weighed
on consumer purchasing power and corporate margins, while
heightened geopolitical risk has increased financial market
volatility, tightened financial conditions, and dampened
investment sentiment globally. The broader global economy has
experienced slower growth momentum and increased downside
risks to the medium‑term outlook, prompting IMF to lower its

term outlook. Demand was primarily driven by technology‑led
transformation initiatives, with investments focused on scaling
AI adoption, modernising core systems and data infrastructure,
enhancing operational efficiency and resilience as well as ensuring
regulatory compliance. Despite a challenging macro environment,

for competitiveness and long‑term transformation.
